newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF expected to discuss Euro-strategy at meeting.
newsitem.headline: MATIF expected to discuss Euro-strategy at meeting.

text.p: The board of France's MATIF futures and options exchange will meet on Tuesday to discuss a number of technical issues which are likely to raise questions of strategy as well after the failure of alliance talks with Germany's stock and options market body.
A spokeswoman for MATIF, Europe's second largest derivatives exchange, said the meeting would discuss "a number of technical matters" but declined to elaborate.

Market sources said, however, that these technical issues were tied to future actions and therefore to a discussion of strategy, as the exchange prepares for tougher international competition with the advent of a single European currency.

Les Echos newspaper said on Monday MATIF chairman Gerard Pfauwadel would present a strategy note to the board which advocated a "dual" organisational structure which effectively ruled out a tie-up with the French stock markets body the Societe des Bourse Francaises (SBF).
With the advent of the single currency in 1999, the MATIF meeting could also raise the subject of new contracts for PIBOR interest rate futures or Notionnel bond futures, Les Echos said.

Cooperation talks between the MATIF pit-trading exchange and the Deutsche Boerse stock and options market failed in August, with the German market rejecting the "open outcry" system and saying it wanted "electronic or nothing".

The MATIF exchange, where more than 80 percent of volume is in interest rate contracts, hopes that European economic and monetary union will give it critical mass as a major trading centre for euro-denominated interest rate contracts.
The French Treasury has already said it plans to start issuing its securities in euros from 1999 and that it will convert the whole stock of existing securities into the euro.
